approach: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, replace `reading_text_fields` with `file_bound_text_fields`, which returns only acceptance criteria of kind `Content`, labelled `acceptance_criteria[i]`. `check_boundary_and_repo_files` scans those and the deliverable paths with `athena_context::briefs::boundary_scan`. Title, summary, decline_reason, question, departures, hard_reason, urgent_reason, assumptions, out_of_scope, defaults_applied and `behavior` criteria are no longer scanned. The repository-file checks and the request-text scan are unchanged. The module docs, doc comments and D153 state the scope and the reason: readings are records outside the policy scan, and the writer gets the word list and runs the scan (D73). They also state, without false backstop claims, the gaps this leaves: criterion kind is an imperfect signal, and the reading's title, summary and criterion texts reach commit messages and the pull request title, which no scan covers. Two test-only departures keep the suite green and pin the rule: run_pin_tests.rs (an end-to-end test asserts the old summary refusal) and the refusal corpus (four boundary-word cases). I do not widen the change to close.rs, run/mod.rs or gh/early.rs. I name the commit-text gap and the fix as an open question for the user.

decisions.choice: Scan only deliverable paths and `content`-kind acceptance criteria; skip `behavior` criteria and all other prose. Criterion kind is the deciding signal.
decisions.reason: A `content` criterion describes file text, so a word there can reach a tracked file. A `behavior` criterion names commands to run. Prose in a record is outside the policy scan (xtask/tests/policy.rs skips records/), and the writer already gets the word list and runs the scan (D73). Kind is the only signal in the `Criterion` struct. It is imperfect in two ways, which the module docs and D153's Tradeoff say: (a) a `content` criterion that describes a document without quoting text is still scanned, so it can be refused with no word reaching a file; (b) a `behavior` criterion that quotes output is not scanned, so the writer could copy a word into a test. Backstops for (b) are the writer's scan (D73) and the policy scan at verification, which both cover tracked files only.

rejected.option: Keep scanning every acceptance criterion and drop only the other prose fields
rejected.why: Behavior criteria are commands and checks, not file text. Scanning them still refuses readings for words that cannot reach a file, and the request and reading say content criteria only.

rejected.option: Remove the word check from readings entirely
rejected.why: A word in a deliverable path or in text a criterion tells the writer to write would reach a file and fail the policy scan at verification. The request keeps the check there.

rejected.option: Special-case the refused requests (allow-list or retry exemption)
rejected.why: The scope of the rule is wrong, so fix the scope. A per-request exception leaves the next prose-only refusal in place (root-cause default).

rejected.option: Change the boundary scan or word list in athena_context::briefs
rejected.why: Out of scope. The scan is the one the policy test runs; only where the reading check applies it changes.

decisions.choice: Do not close the commit-text path in this change. Name it in the module docs and D153's Tradeoff, drop any claim that a backstop covers it, and raise it as an open question for the user.
decisions.reason: Read in run/close.rs: the landing message is `message(&ctx.reading.title, &body, ...)` (line 117; also line 480 for a retried landing), `landing_body` (line 590) starts with `reading.summary.trim()` and lists each `c.criterion`, `closing_subject` (line 564) puts the title in closing commit subjects, and run/mod.rs:1426 passes the title to `early_pr`, which becomes the pull request title (gh/early.rs). The host squash-merges, so this text can become the commit on main. I grepped crates/ for `plain_boundary_text` and `boundary_scan`. Neither is called on these sinks, and xtask has no scan of commit messages (grep for git log, commit message and HISTORY found none). So after this change nothing scans those words on that path, and the policy scan and writer scan do not cover it. The request states its premise as 'a word reaching a tracked file' and asks that a summary holding a word be accepted; it lists three deliverables and 'one focused change'. Closing the gap means sanitizing at about eight title sites in close.rs, run/mod.rs and gh/early.rs. That is a separate behavior change with its own tests, and it is the user's call, not a silent widening.

rejected.option: Sanitize the title, summary and criterion text with `plain_boundary_text` at the commit and pull request sinks, in this change
rejected.why: It is the right follow-up and the critic proposed it, but it adds close.rs, run/mod.rs and gh/early.rs with their own tests to a change meant to be one focused narrowing of one check. It also changes text on the landing path that other tests may pin. I propose it as a separate job and ask the user.

rejected.option: Keep scanning the title and summary to protect the commit path
rejected.why: It reverses the request's required behavior (a summary holding a word is accepted) and is the cause of the repeated refusals.

rejected.why: False: both scan tracked files only. The plan must not imply cover that does not exist.

open_questions: Commit-text gap (critic finding 3): the reading's title, summary and criterion texts reach landing commit messages (run/close.rs lines 117, 480, `landing_body` at 590, `closing_subject` at 564) and the pull request title (run/mod.rs:1426 to gh/early.rs). No scan covers commit messages, and this change removes the only gate on that text. Should a follow-up job run that text through `athena_context::briefs::plain_boundary_text` at those sinks, with a test that a landing message and pull request title pass `boundary_scan`? I recommend yes, as a separate job; this plan does not do it.

A `behavior` criterion could still be copied by the writer into a test name or comment. Criterion 3 accepts this; D153 records it, and the backstops are the writer's scan (D73) and the policy scan at verification.
The counts of six and two refusals come from the request; records are absent from the snapshot, so D153 says they are stated by the request and not measured here.

Reader prompt files may still say every text field is scanned. Prompt files are out of scope; the producer greps crates/athena-context/prompts/ for such a line and reports it in the output without editing it.
